newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki in late come-back after Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki in late come-back after Wall St rise.

text.p: Shares staged a late comeback after a queasy start on Thursday, boosted by gains on Wall St after U.S. November consumer data hit expectations and helped soothe fears of monetary tightening by the federal reserve.
The HEX index ended up 0.13 percent at 2,437.32 with volume back nearer normal levels after Wednesday's record at 2,437.32.

The market was "very nervous" for most of the day, but "investors have money", one broker said, while others pointed towards renewed bullishness once signals of moderate U.S. inflation had come through.
Forestries took a hit but in quite thin dealings when preliminary Norscan pulp figures showed stocks at a high level, but UPM-Kymmene later tracked the market rebound.

Nokia dominated volume, picking up two markka to 263.00, and some brokers attributed a two markka gain in insurer Pohjola -- which attracted heavier than usual trade -- partly to its sizeable stake in the recently recovering telecoms stock.
Pohjola companies at end-1995 held around four percent of Nokia stock. Pohjola closed at 102.00 markka.
Finnlines was also again in focus, with trade heavier than in forestries, but the stock fell one markka to 112.00.
Brokers were generally calm about this weekend's EMU summit, only seeing potential impact on stocks if it raises serious doubts about a single currency.
